> AGENT

The package-root entrypoint idea is sound, but eager imports in `__init__.py` created real cycles in `next↔scan↔status` and `plan↔triage↔review`. I’m converting those exports to lazy wrappers so the package roots stay stable without pulling implementation modules in at import time.

\"\"\"\n+async fn demo() {\n+    let guard = state.lock().await;\n+    work().await;\n+    drop(guard);\n+}\n+\"\"\"\n+    dropped_body = \"\"\"\n+async fn demo() {\n+    let guard = rust_shared_mod._ASYNC_GUARD_ACQUIRE_RE,\n+    ) is True\n+    assert rust_shared_mod._holds_lock_guard_across_await(\n+        dropped_body,\n+        rust_shared_mod._ASYNC_GUARD_ACQUIRE_RE,\n+    )    // safely reconstruct a vec without leaking memory\n+    unsafe { Vec::from_raw_parts(ptr, len, cap) }\n+}\n+\"\"\"\n+    transmute_wrapper = \"\"\"\n+#[repr(transparent)]\n+pub struct Yes. From the current `desloppify plan triage`, `desloppify next`, `desloppify plan queue`, and `desloppify show review --status open`, I can see a few process-level issues:

- Triage state is drifting from the queue. The tool reports `7 new review issue(s) not yet triaged` and also `7 issues not yet in a cluster`, while still presenting a live execution queue. So triage is only partially incorporated, but the execution queue keeps moving anyway.

- Observe judgments are not propagating cleanly. In `show review --status open`, at least two open review issues already carry notes from observe saying they were verified as not worth scheduling this cycle, but they remain open and counted in review debt:

  - `service_role_exempted_by_path` rooted in [signal_patterns.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/base/signal_patterns.py)
  That suggests triage evidence is advisory, not actually resolving/suppressing queue items.

- Queue hygiene is noisy. `next` reports `31` queue items, `plan queue` reports `74 planned`, and `next` also says `2 plan-tracked items are stale and not part of the live queue`. That makes it harder to tell what is truly blocking completion.

- Cluster quality is being validated late. `plan triage` currently says three clusters are missing enough `action_steps`. That implies the process allows under-specified clusters to survive until organize-time instead of enforcing executor-ready shape earlier.

The clearest triage-process bug is the `organize` vs `enrich` gating contradiction. The clearest workflow debt is that triage conclusions are not reliably changing queue state.

> DEVELOPER

Explain the problems holistically please

> AGENT

Holistically, the triage process currently has one core problem: it is not acting like a single authoritative workflow. It has partially overlapping states for review evidence, cluster planning, enrichment, and execution queueing, and those states are drifting apart.

**What’s going wrong**

- The stage model is internally inconsistent. `desloppify plan triage` says the current stage is `organize`, but in the same output it says several clusters must be enriched before `organize` can be recorded. That means the workflow is presenting one stage as active while enforcing prerequisites from a later stage.
- Review intake and triage incorporation are decoupled. The tool reports `7 new review issue(s) not yet triaged`, but it still presents a live execution queue. So new review findings can exist in a limbo state: visible enough to affect status, but not fully incorporated into the plan that `next` is asking you to execute.
- Observe/reflect evidence is not authoritative enough. Some review issues now carry notes saying the observe pass verified they are not worth scheduling this cycle, but those issues are still open and still count in the review backlog. So the human judgment layer can annotate issues without actually changing queue state.
- Plan counts are not coming from one source of truth. Depending on the command, you see different queue numbers and stale-item disclaimers. That usually means one layer is rendering “live actionable queue,” another is rendering “all planned items,” and another still includes stale tracked state. Those views are individually plausible, but together they make it hard to know what “done” means.
- Cluster quality checks are happening too late. The tool allows under-specified clusters to exist until organize-time, then blocks progress because action steps are missing. That means validation is deferred instead of shaping the plan earlier.

**Root cause pattern**

- The system appears to have multiple semi-independent state machines:
  - review findings/import state
  - triage stage state
  - cluster/enrichment state
  - execution queue state
- Those state machines are only loosely synchronized. Instead of one transition making all downstream state consistent, each layer seems to reconcile opportunistically.
- As a result, the process can be “correct” locally in each subsystem while being misleading globally.

**Why this matters**

- It wastes operator effort because you can satisfy one surface and still be blocked by another.
- It weakens trust in `desloppify next`, because “next” may not reflect the full triage reality.
- It makes completion ambiguous. You can’t reliably tell whether the remaining work is real code work, stale triage debt, or queue bookkeeping drift.
- It encourages workaround behavior like force-resolving or manually interpreting the tool’s intent, which defeats the point of the workflow.

**In plain terms**

The triage process is trying to do four jobs at once: judge findings, cluster them, enrich execution steps, and drive the active queue. Right now those jobs are not tightly coupled enough. The tool can tell you “this issue is not worth doing,” “this cluster is not ready,” and “here is your next task” all at the same time without reconciling those statements into one clean plan.

If you want, I can turn this into a concrete defect list for the triage system itself and then keep fixing the queue on top of that.
